lessons.description: Java `for` loops iterate over a range. Implement `sumUpTo(int n)` returning 1 + 2 + ... + n.
learning_objectives: Use standard for loop syntax in Java

lessons.title: 3. Factorial Calculator (Concept Challenge)
lessons.description: Implement factorial(int n) returning n! as a long, using a loop over 1..n. Remember 0! == 1 — the tests check factorial(5) == 120 and factorial(0) == 1.

tests.name: test_factorial
tests.test_code: if (Solution.factorial(5) != 120) throw new AssertionError("5! = 120"); if (Solution.factorial(0) != 1) throw new AssertionError("0! = 1");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — The for Statement
source.license: Oracle Free Use Terms and Conditions (documentation)

lessons.title: 4. Prime Number Checker (Practice)
lessons.description: Implement isPrime(int n): values <= 1 are not prime. Trial-divide by every integer from 2 while i * i <= n; if any divides n evenly it is composite. The tests check 13 is prime and 12 is not.
learning_objectives: Implement primality loop test in Java

tests.name: test_is_prime
tests.test_code: if (!Solution.isPrime(13)) throw new AssertionError("13 is prime"); if (Solution.isPrime(12)) throw new AssertionError("12 is composite");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — The for Statement
source.license: Oracle Free Use Terms and Conditions (documentation)

lessons.description: Implement countEvensInRange(int start, int end): loop from start to end inclusive and count the even numbers (i % 2 == 0). The test expects 5 evens in the range 1..10.
